items.name: HL · Paystack payments → Paid, once
items.what: Paystack's charge.success webhook is answered at once, duplicates stop at a data store check, the payment is verified with Paystack's own API, the amount is compared in kobo, and only then is the order marked Paid with one receipt; a wrong amount emails Tolu instead.
setup: Use Paystack TEST mode and your TEST secret key only. No real money moves.

Data store: create processed_payments with a data structure of order_id (text), amount_kobo (number), processed_at (date). Select it in "Seen this reference?" and "Remember the payment". The record key is the payment reference.

Webhook: in "Paystack webhook" click Add, name it HL Paystack, copy the URL into Paystack → Settings → API Keys & Webhooks → Test Webhook URL. Click "Redetermine data structure" and POST the lesson's sample charge.success JSON from Hoppscotch once so Make learns the fields.
Keychain: in "Verify with Paystack" (HTTP · Make an API Key Auth request) add a keychain: key = Bearer sk_test_… , placement = Header, name = Authorization. Never type the key into a header field.

Connections: open each Google Sheets and Gmail module and choose your Harvest Lane business Google connection (0.6), then pick the spreadsheet (replace YOUR_SHEET_ID) and tab. Gmail sends from the business account; replace tolu@harvestlane.example with Tolu's address.

Column letters: the blueprint assumes Orders = A order_id, B customer_id, C customer_name, D delivery_date, E fee, F status, G items_total, H total (0.4), I phone_clean, J first_name, K delivery_day, L receipt_text (2.2), M paid_at, N channel, O area, P email, Q delivery_window. If yours differ, open each Google Sheets module after import and re-pick the columns.

Optional second layer (Going further): in the webhook's advanced settings turn on "Get request headers" and compare x-paystack-signature with an HMAC-SHA512 of the raw body (sha512(body; ; key) in Make) in a filter right after "Reply 200 ok".
Turn the scenario on (it runs instantly when Paystack calls).
items.test: Run the five tests from the lesson's table: a real test-card payment marks the order Paid, sends one receipt and adds one processed_payments record; resending the same webhook stops at "Not processed before"; a made-up reference POSTed from Hoppscotch stops at "Paystack says success"; a test payment below the order total emails Tolu and leaves the order unpaid; event transfer.success stops at "charge.success only".
build: 1 · Webhooks › Custom webhook "Paystack webhook": new hook HL Paystack; data structure learned from the sample charge.success JSON (event, data.reference, data.amount, data.currency, data.status, data.customer.email, data.metadata.order_id).
2 · Webhooks › Webhook response "Reply 200 ok": Status 200, Body ok.
Filter on 2→3 "charge.success only": {{1.event}} Text operators: Equal to charge.success.
3 · Data store › Check the existence of a record "Seen this reference?": data store processed_payments; Key {{1.data.reference}}.
Filter on 3→4 "Not processed before": Exists (from 3) Boolean operators: Equal to false.

4 · HTTP › Make an API Key Auth request "Verify with Paystack": keychain Authorization: Bearer sk_test_… (Header); URL https://api.paystack.co/transaction/verify/{{1.data.reference}}; Method GET; Parse response Yes; Evaluate all states as errors No (so a fake reference reaches the filter instead of erroring).
Filter on 4→5 "Paystack says success": {{4.data.data.status}} Text operators: Equal to success.
5 · Google Sheets › Search Rows "Find the order": Orders; filter order_id (A) Equal to {{1.data.metadata.order_id}}; Limit 1.
Route 1 · filter on 6→7 "Amount matches (kobo)": {{4.data.data.amount}} Numeric operators: Equal to {{5.total * 100}} (2650000 = 26500 × 100).
7 · Google Sheets › Update a Row "Mark order Paid": Orders; Row number {{5.__ROW_NUMBER__}}; status = Paid; paid_at = {{formatDate(now; "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm")}}; leave other columns empty.

8 · Data store › Add/replace a record "Remember the payment": processed_payments; Key {{1.data.reference}}; Overwrite Yes; order_id {{1.data.metadata.order_id}}, amount_kobo {{4.data.data.amount}}, processed_at {{now}}.

9 · Gmail › Send an email "Send one receipt": To {{1.data.customer.email}}; Subject Payment received · {{5.order_id}}; Content {{5.receipt_text}} (the 2.2 receipt) + "Payment received: ₦{{formatNumber(4.data.data.amount / 100; 0; "."; ",")}} (ref {{1.data.reference}}). Thank you!".
Route 2 · filter on 6→10 "Amount wrong (kobo)": {{4.data.data.amount}} Numeric operators: Not equal to {{5.total * 100}}.

10 · Gmail › Send an email "Alert Tolu: wrong amount": To tolu@harvestlane.example; Subject Partial or wrong payment for {{5.order_id}}; body states the paid amount, the order total and the reference, and that the order was not marked Paid.

walk.title: Build it: payments that confirm themselves, safely
walk.sample: Paystack test charge.success · reference HL-0061-a1 · amount 2,650,000 kobo · order HL-0061 · ₦26,500

steps.say: Everything here runs in Paystack test mode with test keys. No real money moves. First, create a data store called processed_payments, keyed by the payment reference.
The trigger is a custom webhook. Paste its address into Paystack's test webhook setting, and post the sample once so Make learns the fields.
Reply straight away with a two hundred and ok. A fast reply stops Paystack retrying and piling up duplicates.
On the next link, a filter lets only successful charges through. Any other event, like a transfer, stops here.
Now the memory. Check whether we've already handled this reference.
show: Data store › Check the existence of a record

steps.say: Continue only if it's new. A duplicate webhook stops here, before any work or a second receipt.
Never trust the webhook body. We phone Paystack's verify endpoint with the reference. The secret key lives in a keychain, never typed into a header field.
show: HTTP › Make an API Key Auth request · GET

steps.say: Only Paystack's own answer decides. A fake payment someone posted has no successful transaction, so it stops at this filter.
Find the order in the sheet using the order ID we put in the payment's metadata.
A router checks the amount. Paystack counts in kobo, so the order total times a hundred must match exactly.
On the matching route, mark the order Paid with the time.
Then remember the payment in the data store, so if the same webhook ever arrives again, it's harmless.
And send exactly one receipt, reusing the readable receipt text from 2.2.
If the amount is wrong, the other route emails Tolu instead, and the order is not marked Paid.
show: Subject: Partial or wrong payment for {{5.`0`}}

walk.end: Run all five tests: a real test payment, a duplicate, a fake, a wrong amount and another event, and check each stops exactly where it should.
